newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania returns local dealer status to 24 banks.
newsitem.headline: Romania returns local dealer status to 24 banks.

text.p: Romania's central bank (BNR) has restored local dealer licences to 24 banks, which along with the existing four dealers, will act as market makers on the foreign exchange market, BNR governor Mugur Isarescu said.

"All banks which acted as dealers before (March 1996 curbs), except Dacia Felix and Credit Bank, have regained their dealer status," Isarescu told a news conference during which Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea set forth a tough reform package after loan talks with international lenders.

The move ends almost one year of curbs imposed by the former ruling leftists last March when all but four banks lost their local dealer licence. The banks became brokers and had to observe rates imposed by the four dealers, three of which are state-run banks.

Private troubled banks Dacia Felix SA and Renasterea Creditului Romanesc Credit Bank SA, which revealed huge bad debts and losses, now await court rulings on their fate -- liquidation or reorganisation.
The International Monetary Fund cited foreign exchange market restrictions among the main reasons behind its decision to suspend loans for Romania in 1996.

Liberalising the foreign exchange market is part of a tough reform programme launched by Ciorbea's new centrist coalition government, which replaced ex-communists ousted during elections last November.
Isarescu said the BNR would analyse requests for a local dealer licence from another 10 banks, which have been created over the past year.
"If they prove they are able to act as market makers, they will also be licensed as dealers," Isarescu said.
Romania has now 41 commercial banks, nine of which are foreign bank branches.
Isarescu said renewing licences might trigger "disorderly moves" of the leu's exchange rates in the next few days but the liberalised market would eventually help to integrate prices.
Traders said the leu might weaken to some 8,000 to the dollar in the coming days from 7,500/600 at Monday's close. Its retail prices are already hovering at 7,600/8,200.
The leu, kept artificially high in an electoral year last year, has plunged by some 83 percent on the interbank market since January 1. (( -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 310264))
